descriptions: REE-controlled params[0].memref.size flows into obj_id_sz and directly controls TEE_Malloc(obj_id_sz, ...) without any maximum/upper-bound check, enabling untrusted input to drive excessive allocation (resource exhaustion) or extreme-size edge cases.

REE-controlled params[0].memref.size propagates to obj_id_sz and directly controls TEE_Malloc allocation size without any upper-bound check, enabling untrusted input to drive excessive allocation (resource exhaustion / abnormal behavior).

REE-controlled params[0].memref.size is used directly as the allocation size for TEE_Malloc with no upper-bound check, allowing an attacker to request excessively large allocations (resource exhaustion / abnormal behavior).

descriptions: TEE_MemMove uses obj_id_sz (derived from REE-controlled params[0].memref.size) as the copy length, with no visible bounds/range validation beyond successful allocation; the untrusted size directly governs the memory operation length.

obj_id_sz is derived from REE-controlled params[0].memref.size and is used as the copy length in TEE_MemMove from shared memory to a newly allocated buffer, with no explicit maximum/format validation of obj_id_sz (e.g., max object ID length), allowing untrusted length to drive memory operation size.
why_not_categories: Not Unencrypted Data Output: data is copied from untrusted shared memory into private memory, not the other way around.

Not Direct Usage of Shared Memory: the shared buffer is only used as a copy source here; the primary mechanism is untrusted length controlling a memory operation, not a check/use trust decision on shared contents.
Not other: fits IVW based on tainted length reaching a copy primitive without explicit bounds validation.
Not Unencrypted Data Output: data flow is from untrusted shared memory into private memory, not from private secrets to untrusted output.

Not Direct Usage of Shared Memory: the shared buffer is immediately copied to private memory and not subsequently relied upon for decisions without copying; the core issue is unchecked length, not TOCTOU on shared contents.
Not other: fits Input Validation Weakness because an untrusted length controls a memory copy without bounds validation.

descriptions: REE-controlled obj_id_sz (params[0].memref.size) is used directly as the length for TEE_MemMove from shared memory into a newly allocated buffer, with no explicit upper bound on obj_id_sz. This permits untrusted input to drive large allocations/copies and constitutes missing size validation before a memory operation.
why_not_categories: Not Unencrypted Data Output: this is a copy from untrusted shared memory into private memory, not disclosure of a private secret to untrusted-visible memory.
Not Direct Usage of Shared Memory: the shared buffer is only read for copying; the main issue is lack of bounds/size validation on the copy length, not TOCTOU on shared content used for decisions.
Not other: fits the definition of unchecked tainted length in a memory operation.

descriptions: The TA copies data read from a private persistent object into params[1].memref.buffer, which is shared/untrusted-visible memory, without any encryption step; this can disclose application-private stored contents to the REE.

Data read from a persistent object in private storage is copied into params[1].memref.buffer, which is REE-shared/untrusted-visible memory, without any encryption step. This directly exposes application-private stored contents to the untrusted side.

The function copies data read from a persistent object (trusted/private storage contents) into params[1].memref.buffer, which is shared memory visible to the REE. No encryption is performed before the TEE_MemMove, so private application data is output in plaintext to an untrusted-visible region.
